entry.title: HoloCT: a 3D foundation model for both CT reading and segmentation
entry.summary: A 3D foundation model unifying CT interpretation and segmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents HoloCT, a general 3D foundation model that combines CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation, providing 3D masks as evidence. The authors built HoloDATA from 195,921 CT scans and compared the model across 346 tasks against specialist and foundation models. In multicentre validation on 11,455 clinical scans from five hospitals, HoloCT outperformed competing models in lesion segmentation and report generation. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors unify CT interpretation and voxel-level segmentation in one 3D model, reporting gains over specialist and foundation models across 346 tasks.

entry.title: AI-assisted classification when people ignore overlapping evidence and mistrust AI
entry.summary: AI-Assisted Classification under Correlation Neglect and Trust arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines when an AI assistant helps or harms human decisions, arguing that outcomes depend on how much the AI's evidence overlaps with the human's and how the human combines them, not just on AI accuracy. The authors build a behavioral model with two parameters, awareness of overlap and trust in the AI, and derive a phase diagram of complementarity, impairment and automation regions. On ChatBench, AI assistance raises accuracy by 21 points, yet workers use only about a quarter of the Bayes-rational weight on AI information. Calibrating trust recovers about 2.6 points for GPT-4o but almost nothing for Llama-3.1-8b. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model correlation neglect and trust in human-AI decisions, derive a closed-form phase diagram, and report decomposing accuracy loss on ChatBench.

entry.title: Using topology to classify all mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions
entry.summary: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies mutually unbiased bases (MUBs), which are complementary quantum measurements in which certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. Using the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, the authors classify all sets of MUBs in dimension six. They show that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix, which implies that no four MUBs exist. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use topological connectedness to classify all mutually unbiased triples in dimension six and report that no fourth basis exists.

entry.title: Efficient quantum ultraspherical transform and a well-conditioned quantum spectral method: a transform and spectral solver for solving linear differential equations on quantum computers.
entry.summary: Efficient quantum ultraspherical transform and a well-conditioned quantum spectral method arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper constructs a quantum ultraspherical transform (QUT) for orthonormal ultraspherical polynomials, converting between amplitudes of function values and expansion coefficients. For each fixed integer m≥2 and dimensions with N+m=2^n, the transform achieves error at most ε with a gate count polynomial in n and log(1/ε), built on the quantum Fourier transform. Using the QUT, the authors develop a quantum spectral solver for regular linear ordinary differential equations, where preconditioning keeps condition numbers bounded independently of basis size under suitable assumptions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a quantum ultraspherical transform for all integer m≥2 and a spectral solver for linear ODEs with bounded preconditioned condition numbers.

entry.title: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models to improve decoding
entry.summary: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models improving decoding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a data-driven method that discovers new error mechanisms directly from experimental detector-firing statistics to augment detector error models (DEMs) for quantum error correction. Candidates are built by combining pairs of existing mechanisms and then filtered using pairwise and higher-order detector correlations. In surface-code simulations with correlated noise, the augmented model raised the Lambda parameter by 20% and cut the logical error rate by 75% at code distance 15. On Google superconducting device data, it raised Lambda by 9% and reduced the logical error rate by 14% at distance 7. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report discovering new correlated error mechanisms from experimental detector statistics with assigned logical effects, validated on surface-code simulations and Google superconducting dat

entry.title: Compatibility of Pauli Observables: A study of whether one measurement can approximate several Pauli observables
entry.summary: Compatibility of Pauli Observables arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how sharply a single measurement can approximate an arbitrary finite family of Pauli observables, and what sharpness tradeoffs result. The authors derive an exact state-space correspondence linking incompatibility to preparation uncertainty, and they construct explicit parent measurements via Pauli conjugation and classical randomisation. The paper also shows that magic is necessary to reach the full compatibility region of every noncommuting Pauli family. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a state-space correspondence characterising Pauli compatibility regions, linking incompatibility to preparation uncertainty and showing magic is necessary, with exact results reported

entry.title: Equivalence of correlated catalytic and marginal asymptotic transformations in quantum resource theories
entry.summary: Equivalence of Correlated Catalytic and Marginal Asymptotic Transformations in Quantum Resource Theories arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proves that correlated-catalytic state conversion is possible exactly when the marginal asymptotic conversion rate is at least one. The equivalence holds for arbitrary states across broad classes of entanglement, coherence, and magic theories. Under local operations and classical communication, the authors fully characterize conversion from arbitrary bipartite states to entangled pure states via distillable entanglement. They show that correlated catalysts cannot increase distillable entanglement or distillable secret key, nor make bound entanglement distillable. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove correlated-catalytic conversion is equivalent to marginal asymptotic rate at least one, extending to distillable entanglement and secret key results.

entry.title: Whether energy gaps of quantum matter survive weak local perturbations, given only locality and translation invariance
entry.summary: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the stability of energy gaps in macroscopic quantum many-body systems, assuming only locality and translation invariance. The authors show that in any spatial dimension there exist gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state whose gap becomes unstable, closing under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbations in the thermodynamic limit. For one-dimensional spin and fermionic systems, such unstable-gap Hamiltonians must break translation invariance and be fine-tuned. In dimensions greater than one, fine-tuned translation-invariant local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and unstable gap are shown to exist. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show existence of gapped local Hamiltonians with unique ground state but unstable gap in any dimension, with one-dimensional characterizations.

entry.title: Shadow bootstrapping: pure-state tomography with few measurement settings
entry.summary: Shadow bootstrapping: Nearly minimal-setting pure-state tomography with shallow Clifford measurements arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a method for reconstructing unknown pure quantum states using nearly the fewest possible measurement settings. The algorithm uses single-copy, nonadaptive shallow Clifford measurements, each implemented by a circuit of depth O(log n), and achieves optimal sample complexity. Its key technique, shadow bootstrapping, uses the current estimate to reduce the variance of later residual estimates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose shadow bootstrapping, achieving near-minimal measurement settings and optimal sample complexity for pure-state tomography with shallow Clifford measurements.

entry.title: Operator-norm bounds on sums of positive operators, with applications to quantum games and key distribution
entry.summary: Norm Bounds on Sums of Positive Operators with Applications to Monogamy Games and Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proves a general inequality bounding the operator norm of averages of positive semidefinite operators, which can be used to bound quantum measurement acceptance probabilities. It applies this to the parallel BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement game, identifying the robustness threshold at which the optimal winning probability decays exponentially or stays bounded away from zero. It also shows that one-sided device-independent BB84 quantum key distribution achieves any asymptotic key rate below 1 minus 2 times the binary entropy of the tolerated bit-error rate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a general operator-norm inequality for sums of positive operators and apply it to sharp thresholds in parallel BB84 monogamy games and one-sided device-independent QKD rates.

entry.title: Algorithmic wave-particle duality: finding paths in welded trees is hard
entry.summary: Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the welded trees problem, in which an algorithm must navigate a randomly labeled graph made of two binary trees joined at their leaves, from one root to the other. Quantum walks can do this exponentially faster than any classical method, but recording the path destroys the interference behind that speedup. The authors prove that, for trees of height n, finding a root-to-root path with constant probability requires quantum query complexity Θ̃(2^{n/3}), and that this bound is tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a tight quantum query bound of 2^(n/3) for finding root-to-root paths in welded trees, using the compressed permutation oracle.

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Quantum Estimation With Persistent Memory
entry.summary: Structural Lower Bounds for Quantum Property Estimation with Persistent Memory arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies quantum property estimation, where an experimenter estimates expectation values of a family of observables from independent copies of an unknown state to additive error ε. The authors develop a backward-induction framework based on operator resolvents, reducing the lower bound to an algebraic certificate computed from the target observables with Ω(1/ε²) scaling. For a persistent memory of dimension K, they show lower bounds that match memoryless or commuting estimators within polylogarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a resolvent-based backward induction reducing persistent-memory lower bounds to algebraic certificates, with tight bounds for Pauli and Majorana estimation.

entry.title: Learning quantum dynamics despite unknown state preparation and measurement errors
entry.summary: SPAM-robust learnability of quantum dynamics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies which properties of quantum dynamics can still be learned when state preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors are unknown. It treats quantum channels and continuous-time evolution in one framework, using the cycle structure of a generalized pattern-transfer graph to characterize all learnable parameter combinations and building explicit SPAM-robust learning protocols. It also shows that coherent structure greatly restricts gauge ambiguity, making coherent coefficients and broad classes of dissipative error parameters individually learnable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize learnable parameters via cycle structure of a generalized pattern-transfer graph, and show coherent structure reduces continuous gauge freedom to discrete or trivial choices.

entry.title: Fermionic analogue of the Porter-Thomas distribution and how it arises in random matchgate circuits
entry.summary: Fermionic Porter-Thomas statistics and their emergence in random matchgate circuits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper derives the measurement-probability distribution for random fermionic Gaussian states, with and without particle-number conservation, which is the fermionic counterpart of the Porter-Thomas law. For large systems the probabilities become log-normally distributed with moments growing polynomially in system size. The authors also show how this distribution emerges in random one-dimensional brickwork matchgate circuits and prove depth requirements for the collision probability to converge. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an exact Porter-Thomas analogue for random fermionic Gaussian states and its emergence in matchgate circuits, with a proof on convergence depth.

entry.title: FrontierPhysics: A Benchmark for Agents Doing End-to-End Physics Research
entry.summary: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FrontierPhysics, a benchmark of 56 tasks written by 42 physicists from their own research, spanning nine domains of theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Agents must review literature, plan research, conduct experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Evaluation combines deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics to judge correctness and publishability. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passed more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce an end-to-end benchmark of 56 physicist-authored research tasks across nine domains, reporting that no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts.

entry.title: Simulation-trained humanoid robot motion driven by vision and language (HALO system)
entry.summary: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents HALO, a humanoid robot system that acts on visual and language inputs. It generates vision-language-motion training data across a thousand procedurally generated virtual homes, so data scales with computing rather than human effort. HALO learns skills such as sitting on chairs, navigating to named objects, passing sideways through half-open doors, crawling under tables, and pushing boxes, and combines them for long-horizon tasks. Without training on any real home, it reached a 91% success rate over 360 trials in six unmapped real-world environments. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors synthesize vision-language-motion data in simulation and report 91% zero-shot success over 360 trials in six real environments.

entry.title: Using reinforcement learning to improve a general robot policy across many tasks
entry.summary: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper asks whether generalist robot policies can be improved online during deployment across many diverse tasks at once. The authors build structured evaluations and systematically compare choices in value estimation, policy extraction, and resource allocation. They report that the right recipe improves policies across diverse tasks and can also raise performance on tasks not seen during online training, with the training task distribution and value-based RL identified as critical. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors study online RL improvement of generalist robot policies across many tasks, reporting generalization to unseen tasks.

entry.title: Improved Randomized Online Matching Beyond 0.55 Competitive Ratio
entry.summary: Online Edge-Weighted Matching Beyond 0.55 arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a randomized algorithm for edge-weighted online bipartite matching with free disposal, achieving a competitive ratio of 0.556195. This improves on the previous 0.5368 guarantee by Blanc and Charikar. The algorithm builds on online correlated selection and is analyzed with a state-dependent primal-dual method, with some selection inequalities verified by a computer-assisted proof whose verifiers are publicly available. The authors also show that triangular unit-weight inputs asymptotically attain the guarantee of the underlying ideal algorithm, indicating the analysis is tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the competitive ratio for edge-weighted online bipartite matching to 0.556 via state-dependent primal-dual analysis with computer-assisted verification and a tight bound.

entry.title: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Strict Separation at 1-1/e
entry.summary: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Strict Separation at 1-1/e arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies online allocation where element values are drawn independently and revealed in random order, with the goal of choosing an independent set or disjoint buyer bundles compared against the expected offline optimum. For matroids, the authors give a randomized algorithm achieving a (1-1/e+10^-6) competitive ratio with polynomial running time in the independence-oracle model. For combinatorial auctions with XOS valuations, they show 1-1/e is the optimal competitive ratio, establishing a strict separation between the two settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matroid prophet-secretary beats 1-1/e and give a tight 1-1/e bound for XOS auctions, a notable separation result.

entry.title: Linear-time recovery of erased bits in quantum expander codes
entry.summary: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Small-Set-Peeling, a quantum generalization of the classical Peeling decoder for erasure errors in quantum expander codes. The decoder can correct up to D−1 erasures, where D is the design distance of the code, and it is guaranteed to run in linear time. Combined with the erasure-conversion algorithm Small-Set-Find, the authors also obtain a graph-local linear-time decoder for Pauli errors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize the classical Peeling decoder to quantum expander codes, reporting the first guaranteed linear-time correction of D-1 erasures, combined with erasure conversion for Pauli errors

entry.title: A quantum lower bound for finding triangles in graphs
entry.summary: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies triangle finding, a basic graph problem where the input is an N-vertex graph given by its adjacency matrix. The best known quantum query upper bound was O(N^{5/4}), while the best lower bound was the basic Ω(N) from unstructured search. The authors prove that Ω(N^{13/12}) quantum queries are necessary, the first superlinear quantum query lower bound for this problem. The same bound also holds for triangle detection and for detecting any fixed connected non-bipartite graph. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first superlinear quantum query lower bound Ω(N^{13/12}) for triangle finding, using compressed oracles and transfer methods.

entry.title: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling
entry.summary: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies truthful scheduling on unrelated machines and proves that every deterministic truthful fractional mechanism has worst-case approximation ratio at least (n+1)/2, matching the known upper bound. Because truthful-in-expectation mechanisms induce truthful fractional mechanisms, the same lower bound extends to all truthful-in-expectation and universally truthful mechanisms. The authors also give a universally truthful mechanism with approximation ratio n/2+o(n). Together, the results establish that the optimal leading constant for randomized truthful scheduling is 1/2. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve a longstanding open problem, proving a (n+1)/2 lower bound for truthful fractional scheduling and matching randomized upper bounds asymptotically.

entry.title: Private mean estimation without known covariance cannot avoid dimension dependence
entry.summary: Dimension-Free Private Mean Estimation is Impossible Without the Covariance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the limits of differentially private Gaussian mean estimation when the covariance matrix is unknown. When the covariance is known, optimal sample complexity depends only on its spectrum rather than the ambient dimension. The authors prove that private estimators cannot achieve similar guarantees when the covariance is unknown. They give lower bounds showing error gaps of order √(d/n) when the sample size is below the effective dimension, and of order √d/n^{3/2} above it, even for diagonal covariances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove dimension-dependent lower bounds for private Gaussian mean estimation with unknown covariance, contrasting the known-covariance case.

entry.title: Proves that computing competitive equilibrium for linear chores is CLS-complete
entry.summary: Competitive Equilibrium for Linear Chores is CLS-complete arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of finding an exact competitive equilibrium in Fisher markets with divisible chores and linear disutilities. Linear goods markets admit strongly polynomial-time algorithms, but no polynomial-time algorithm was known for linear chores. The authors prove the problem is CLS-hard and therefore CLS-complete, which they claim is the first such result for a market equilibrium problem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show computing exact CE for linear chores is CLS-complete, via reduction from KKT points of a quadratic program.

entry.title: "Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains" introduces how a signed third-party tool can hide code that leaks data, and proposes isolated execution to limit disclosure
entry.summary: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper shows that third-party tools used by AI agents, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, can be authenticated yet still secretly leak confidential data while performing their advertised function. The authors demonstrate this with a signed MCP tool and test MCPGuard-Dynamic, a runtime defence. They propose germline execution, in which each tool call runs in a temporary copy forked from a data-free process and receives only information authorised for its destination. Across 153 attack runs, no unauthorised disclosure was detected under this approach. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose germline execution, forking ephemeral data-isolated copies to bound leakage, and report 153 attack runs compared against baseline defences.

entry.title: Same Scale, Four Texts: Gaps and Hidden Fixes in Published Eye Grading Rules
entry.summary: One Scale, Four Texts: Gaps, Overlaps and Silent Repairs in Published Grading Schemes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper uses diabetic retinopathy grading to examine four texts of one international scale, translating them into a common rule language and enumerating over 1.4 billion finding profiles to find eyes left without a category, overlapping classes, and conflicting orderings. It compares referral decisions across the texts on public photographs and in a pre-registered experiment. It also tests whether language models silently repair gaps when reading the rules. ★★★★ Notable: The authors transcribe four diabetic retinopathy grading texts into one rule language, enumerate finding profiles exhaustively, and report pre-registered experiments on 927 annotated photographs.

entry.title: Signed but Steerable: Closing the Text-Vector Gap in Offline RAG
entry.summary: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies offline retrieval-augmented generation on edge devices, where signed knowledge packs contain both text and precomputed embedding vectors. It shows that a signature proves only who published a pack, not that the vectors match the text. The authors find that verifiers accepting vectors within a cosine tolerance let an attacker controlling the vectors hijack a measurable share of queries across five corpora and two embedding models. They propose verifying quantisation codes instead, and release code and data. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show signatures prove publisher identity but not text-vector consistency, quantify hijack rates via angular margins across corpora and models, and propose quantisation-code verification.

entry.title: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits: Studying bandit problems where options are judged by prospect theory instead of average reward
entry.summary: Risk-Sensitive Non-Parametric and Kernel Bandits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies non-parametric bandits in which arms are evaluated with Cumulative Prospect Theory rather than expected reward, in continuous action spaces with arm-dependent noise. It proposes NPCB, an optimistic algorithm that separates mean estimation from CPT-based decisions, and proves a regret order matching classical non-parametric bandits. The authors extend the method to unknown noise CDFs and derive information-gain-based regret bounds for Kernel-CPT bandits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend CPT risk-sensitive bandits to non-parametric and kernel settings, reporting regret bounds matching risk-neutral rates up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: How many sorted projections are needed to pin down n points in k dimensions?
entry.summary: How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how many directions are needed so that sorted projections of a multiset of n points in k-dimensional space uniquely determine the points. The authors show that in every dimension, almost every choice of (4k-2)ln(2n)ln(k log₂2n)+k+1 directions suffices. For k at most 10 and large n, this beats the previously known linear bound. Improved results for the planar case are also given. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt Hair and Sahai's list-recovery lemmas to give a higher-dimensional direction bound and improve the planar lower-bound constant, with numerical checks reported.

entry.title: Weaver: a method that speeds up blockchain transactions by running them in parallel without waiting for state data.
entry.summary: Weaver: Unlocking Blockchain Transaction Parallelism through State-Decoupled Symbolic Execution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Weaver, a transaction processing approach that lets execution continue before concrete state values are fetched. It represents states as symbolic references, predicts branch directions through hierarchical symbolic pattern matching, and schedules individual expressions as soon as their dependencies are resolved. Evaluated on real Ethereum blocks and synthetic workloads from four dApps, it achieves 41% to 63% higher throughput than state-of-the-art parallel engines and up to 7.5 times that of serial execution. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decouple state access via symbolic references and expression-granular scheduling, reporting throughput gains on real Ethereum blocks and four dApp workloads.

entry.title: Research on re-enabling secure debug on the RP2350 using photon-emission microscopy and laser fault injection
entry.summary: Shoot on (Core)Sight: Re-enabling Secure Debug on the RP2350 with Photon-Emission Microscopy and Laser Fault Injection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the RP2350A4 chip using differential photon-emission microscopy (PEM) and laser fault injection (LFI). PEM narrowed the laser scanning area, revealing two sites where laser pulses set the DEBUGEN bits and enabled core 1 Secure debug. An online attack sequence using only Serial Wire Debug (SWD) feedback restored sustained access, and after a rescue reset it recovered a 128-bit test secret. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine photon-emission microscopy with laser fault injection to flip RP2350 DEBUGEN bits and regain Secure debug, reporting recovery of a 128-bit test secret on the RP2350A4.

entry.title: A physics-based catchment model that rivals deep learning on three continents
entry.summary: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes CaRT, a low-dimensional catchment model constrained by conservation, dissipation and aggregation laws, and refines it with AI agents into CaRT+, which has 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments in held-out years, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765, comparable to LSTM models, though three-seed LSTM ensembles stay slightly ahead. On 505 drier Australian catchments unused in development, a single CaRT+ model scores 0.778, above two LSTMs at 0.762 and 0.753. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a low-dimensional physics-based catchment model, refine it with AI agents, and report LSTM-comparable accuracy across three continents.

entry.title: On the Existence and Complexity of Quasi-strict Equilibria
entry.summary: On Existence and Computational Complexity of Quasi-strict Equilibria arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Quasi-strict Nash equilibrium, introduced by Harsanyi in 1973, requires every pure best response to be played with positive probability. The paper gives a simpler proof that every bimatrix game has such an equilibrium, avoiding a complicated limit argument in Norde's original proof. This proof settles the complexity of computing one by showing the problem is in PPAD. For games with three or more players, the paper shows that deciding whether a quasi-strict equilibrium exists is ∃R-complete, strengthening an earlier NP-hardness result. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a simpler existence proof, resolve PPAD membership for computing quasi-strict equilibria, and show existence deciding for three or more players is ∃R-complete.

entry.title: Faster Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms Built on Multiplication
entry.summary: Improved Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms from Multiplication arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The quantum Fourier transform is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, including Shor's factoring algorithm and phase estimation. The paper reduces the gate count of exact QFT circuits to O(q log q), improving on earlier bounds. It also shows that a multiplication circuit with O(n(log n)^α) gates yields a QFT circuit with O(q(log q)^α) gates. For approximate QFT, the paper further improves the gate count bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give improved gate-count bounds for exact and approximate QFT by transferring multiplication circuit complexity to QFT circuits.

entry.title: Automatically generating training datasets that cause surprising side effects on model behavior
entry.summary: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes automatically discovering datasets with surprising side effects (DSSEs) to study how training data affects language model behavior outside its training domain. The authors search for such datasets using LLM judges, evolutionary search, reinforcement learning, and subliminal learning, followed by re-scoring with held-out metrics. The pipeline yields 6,575 datasets across 8 behaviors, many of which generalize across model families and sizes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose automatically discovering datasets with surprising side effects, producing 6,575 datasets across 8 behaviors using LLM judges and several search methods.

entry.title: Exact memory-rate tradeoff for three-user secure coded caching
entry.summary: The Exact Memory-Rate Tradeoff for Three-User Secure Coded Caching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper determines the exact zero-error memory-rate tradeoff for secure coded caching with three users and any number N≥2 of independent files. Each user recovers its requested file, while its cache and the broadcast jointly reveal no information about the complete tuple of unrequested files. For N≥4, two converse bounds confirm the optimality of known achievable points and the memory-sharing segments between them. For N=3, two additional bounds identify a new corner point at (M,R)=(3/2,2), and an explicit linear code over F_3 achieves it, lowering the rate by one quarter of a file compared with memory sharing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors exactly characterize the three-user secure caching tradeoff, identify a new corner at (3/2,2), and give an explicit F_3 linear code achieving it.

entry.title: Split Protocol Changes Results in Encrypted Traffic Classification Re-evaluation
entry.summary: The Split Protocol Decides the Result: Re-Evaluating Encrypted Traffic Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Encrypted traffic classifiers are often reported at 95-99% accuracy. On one public corpus, the same model scores macro-F1 0.992 under the standard literature protocol but 0.567 when flows from one packet capture stay on one side of the split. The paper also proposes a diagnostic using a single capture identifier to determine which split axis to use before training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that the split protocol drives reported accuracy in encrypted traffic classification, proposing single-identifier probes as a diagnostic. entry.title: NextGAN: A Simpler, Scalable GAN Training Method for Image and Video Generation
entry.summary: NextGAN: Towards Simple and Scalable GAN Training for Image and Video Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents NextGAN, an adversarial training method that trains a scalar critic by regressing its input gradient onto displacements between paired reference and generated features in frozen representation spaces, directly shaping the generator's update gradients. The same objective adapts pre-trained image and video generators with up to 14B parameters without auxiliary losses or online teacher scores. The authors report one-step FIDs of 2.87 (pixel space) and 1.54 (latent space) on ImageNet 256×256, and the highest VBench total scores among compared 1.3B text-to-video methods at one and two steps. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors regress a scalar critic's input gradient onto feature displacements, equivalent to an adversarial objective with gradient-energy penalty; they report gains on ImageNet 256 and Wan2.1-1.3B

entry.title: Pseudo-Riemannian Manifold Learning for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signatures
entry.summary: Learning Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds for Heterophilic Graphs via Graph Signature arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses heterophilic graphs, where connected nodes often have different labels, by introducing a Graph Signature Index that measures the mismatch with positive-definite geometric priors, computed from the inertia of a label-based class-compatibility matrix. The authors prove that no homophily index value in (0,1) rules out a negative eigenvalue. They propose the Pseudo-Riemannian Attention Network (PRAT), whose attention uses a signed squared pseudo-distance under a learnable diagonal metric initialized from the signature. PRAT matches or outperforms the strongest heterophily-adapted models across fifteen node-classification benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a graph signature index and a pseudo-Riemannian attention network, reporting matched or better node classification on fifteen heterophilic benchmarks plus a controlled ablation on

entry.title: Separation as Riesz Energy: How Many Environments ICA Needs
entry.summary: Separation Is a Riesz Energy: How Many Environments Does ICA Need? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper asks whether independent components can be recovered when all are Gaussian, using joint diagonalization of covariances across multiple environments. Each component's variance pattern across environments defines a Riesz 2-energy that measures how hard it is to separate. The authors derive sample-size bounds as the number of components grows, showing the required samples depend on the dimension spanned by these patterns rather than on the number of environments. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use Riesz energy to characterize separation cost, giving a dimension law with tight bounds, and report simulations up to d=1000.

entry.title: Simulating word-RAM programs efficiently with stable population protocols
entry.summary: Efficient Stable Word-RAM Simulation by Population Protocols arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies population protocols, in which indistinguishable agents interact in random pairs, and shows how they can simulate word-RAM programs efficiently. For every polynomial-size word-RAM program, the construction is stable and silent, with stabilisation in polylogarithmic time both in expectation and with high probability. The framework supports multiple outputs, showing that efficient stable protocols compute beyond semilinear predicates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a stable, silent, efficient population protocol simulating polynomial word-RAM programs, beyond semilinear predicates, with polylogarithmic stabilisation time in expectation and w.h.p

entry.title: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks and a Persistent Core
entry.summary: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks and a Persistent Core arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies a balanced random stable-marriage market in which one fixed woman misreports preferences in men-proposing deferred acceptance to secure her best attainable partner. The authors prove that her expected average true partner rank is asymptotic to (ln n)^2, improving the previous O((ln n)^4) bound, while the men's average rank is asymptotic to n/(2ln n). After normalization, the two average ranks converge jointly in distribution to (U, U^{-1}), where U is uniform on (0,1). ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the expected rank bound for one manipulating woman in stable matching and give joint distributional convergence results.

entry.title: SafeStart: Fixing the Overlooked Safety Cost of Running Fewer Experts in MoE Model Serving
entry.summary: SafeStart: Mitigating the Overlooked Safety Cost of Active Expert Reduction in MoE LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper shows that speeding up Mixture-of-Experts language models by running fewer experts per token can weaken their refusal of harmful requests. The authors introduce SafeStart, which uses all experts for the prompt and the first eight generated tokens, and reduced experts only afterward. The method keeps most of the speedup while largely restoring refusal behavior, and the authors argue that refusal should be tested alongside accuracy before such serving methods are enabled. ★★★★ Notable: The authors locate refusal loss from expert reduction in the first generated tokens and propose running all experts there, tested across several MoE models and jailbreak settings.

entry.title: KVGuard: A Safety Checker for the Memory Cache That Stores Language Model Context
entry.summary: KVGuard: A KV Cache Safety Checker for LLM Serving Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Large language model serving systems split their KV cache into fixed-size blocks, which can cause memory bugs such as double-frees, use-after-free errors, and out-of-bounds access that silently corrupt outputs without crashing. This paper presents KVGuard, which keeps shadow metadata for each KV block and runs five safety checks across allocation, block table handling, and GPU-side access. A prototype on vLLM and SGLang covers 29 historical real-world KV cache bugs and found 8 previously unknown safety violations, with no false positives reported. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present a systematic KV cache memory-safety framework with five checks, validated on vLLM and SGLang, covering 29 historical bugs and finding 8 new ones.

entry.title: SenTrojan: Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors
entry.summary: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents SenTrojan, a framework for hidden analog hardware Trojans implanted into sensor circuitry before deployment. The Trojan is activated by crafted external physical signals and can cause malfunctions ranging from denial-of-service to spoofing. Two designs are introduced, a Logic-Rule-Driven and a Physical-Effect-Driven variant, and the authors evaluate them on 14 sensors across 6 transduction principles, reporting an average trigger success rate above 95%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors with two complementary designs, a new threat model; the abstract reports results on 14 sensors across 6 transduction principles.

entry.title: Two-sided screening: how platforms design quality, price and wage menus in differentiated markets
entry.summary: Two-Sided Screening in Quality-Differentiated Markets arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Motivated by platforms such as Uber and Airbnb, this paper studies how a two-sided platform designs a menu of qualities, consumer prices and provider wages when both sides self-select based on private values and costs. The authors characterize profit- and welfare-optimal trading distributions and show that production technology alone can reduce menu size without losing optimal profit or welfare. They also prove that under monotone hazard rate conditions a profit-optimal menu achieves at least 1/(e-1) of optimal welfare, and they give a polynomial-time algorithm for restricted menu sizes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine two-sided screening with quality menu design, characterize optimal trading distributions via convexification, and report a 1/(e-1) welfare approximation for profit-optimal menus.

entry.title: Constant-round parallel algorithms for approximate minimum spanning trees in metric spaces
entry.summary: Constant-Round Massively Parallel Algorithms for Approximate MSTs in Metric Spaces arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for computing approximate minimum spanning trees in metric spaces under the fully scalable Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. It gives results for general metrics, Euclidean spaces, and doubling metrics, specifying the approximation ratio, number of rounds, and space usage for each. For general metrics, the round complexity is asymptotically optimal in its dependence on the error parameter, and the work answers an open question from STOC'23. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a unified framework yielding constant-round MPC approximate MSTs, with a round bound matching a stated lower bound in epsilon.

entry.title: Catastrophic overfitting as weight drift invisible to training loss
entry.summary: Catastrophic Overfitting is Weight Drift the Training Loss Cannot See arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Fast adversarial training uses a single-step attack instead of a multi-step one to cut costs, but partway through training its robustness to multi-step attacks collapses, a phenomenon called catastrophic overfitting. The paper argues this is a quiet drift of the network weights, since the training objective barely changes while most robustness is lost. The exponential moving average of the weights does not drift and stays robust throughout, so the authors reset weights to this average when validation robustness drops. Built on a coupling-based method, the approach removes catastrophic overfitting in all runs and achieves the strongest AutoAttack accuracy among fast methods on three benchmark datasets. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast catastrophic overfitting as training-loss-invisible weight drift and propose resetting to EMA weights; the abstract reports results on three benchmarks.

entry.title: Breaking the One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair for Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria
entry.summary: Breaking the One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair for Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies polynomial-time algorithms for approximate Nash equilibria in multiplayer games, where prior methods relying on one-player extension could only improve the classical 1-1/m guarantee to 1-1/(m-c). The authors propose an iterative descent-and-repair framework that directly handles general m-player games and achieves a 1-(σ⋆-ε)/m approximation for sufficiently large m, where σ⋆ ≈ 1.5867. A new potential function inspired by continuous-time dynamics certifies progress across iterations and ensures polynomial-time termination. ★★★★ Notable: The authors break the long-standing one-player extension barrier for multiplayer approximate Nash equilibria via a history-aware iterative repair framework, with polynomial-time termination proved for

entry.title: Learning auction reserve prices from censored past bids offline
entry.summary: Offline Learning of Reserve Prices from Censored Bids arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how a seller can learn a second-price auction reserve price from historical bid data where low values are censored. Under a monotone hazard rate assumption, it characterizes exactly when the optimal reserve is identified. When it is not, the authors derive the reserve minimizing worst-case revenue regret across distributions consistent with the data, and show it depends on two observable quantities. Experiments on synthetic and eBay data compare the approach with parametric models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize identifiability of reserve prices from censored bids, derive minimax reserves with regret bounds, and report experiments on synthetic and eBay data.

entry.title: Softmax Attention at Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds
entry.summary: Softmax Attention with Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching the Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of attention, the core operation in modern AI models. For fixed dimension d, it gives an algorithm for m queries and n key-value pairs with expected time near (mn)^{k/(k+1)} + m + n, where k = floor(d/2). When m = n and d is at least 2, the bound is near n^{2-2/(floor(d/2)+1)}, improving the previous n^{2-1/d} upper bound. The result matches the best known batch maximum-inner-product bounds in each fixed dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the complexity upper bound for softmax attention in fixed dimension and match the best known batch maximum-inner-product bound, plus a reduction.

entry.title: PIMROP: Feasibility of Return-Oriented Programming on Commercial Processing-in-Memory Chips
entry.summary: PIMROP: A Feasibility Study of Return-Oriented Programming on Commercial Processing-in-Memory Architectures arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies code-reuse attacks on processing-in-memory (PIM) hardware, where small programmable cores sit beside DRAM banks. The authors target the commercial UPMEM DPU instruction set, build a gadget scanner adapted to its fixed-width encoding, and find 517 usable gadgets in its runtime library. They demonstrate two verified end-to-end attacks that leak a secret, and show that stack canaries and fortification fail on this platform. A bounds-checked DMA is shown to stop the attack, and the tools are open-sourced. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first code-reuse attack on the commercial UPMEM DPU PIM ISA, with two end-to-end attacks on a functional simulator.

entry.title: Who Pays for Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
entry.summary: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies why generative models trained on earlier models' outputs lose knowledge over generations, rare knowledge first. The authors reframe model collapse as Rogers' paradox, arguing that a population relying on copying is no better off than one that never copied unless people keep learning for themselves. They test this with Rogers' model on language models and extend it to changing worlds and to feedback loops where people ask models instead of finding things out. They conclude that only checks that bring in new information act as critical learning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reframe model collapse as Rogers' paradox, test Rogers' model on trigram and pretrained transformer language models, and analyze an equilibrium with endogenous fresh-data supply.

entry.title: From Waste to Discovery: Reusing Highly Scored Unshown Items in Taobao Feed Recommendations
entry.summary: From Waste to Discovery: Recycling High-Scored Unexposed Candidates in Taobao Feed Recommendation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents URED, a training-free system that recycles items scored highly by recommenders but never shown to users, reintroducing them at the recall stage of Taobao feed recommendation. Online A/B tests report a 3.47% increase in discovered categories and an 8.47% gain in content richness, with engagement preserved. Ablation studies indicate that both the 30-day aggregation window and score-based filtering are necessary for the gains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recycle high-scored unexposed candidates instead of boosting discovery exposure, reporting Taobao online A/B tests with gains in discovered categories and richness.

entry.title: Decoupling Pretrained Knowledge for Reuse in Time Series Forecasting Models
entry.summary: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of adapting pretrained time series foundation models to downstream tasks because of domain shifts. It proposes FKA, a two-stage framework that decouples pretraining knowledge into compact, task-shared residual codebooks for trend and seasonal signals, and uses them to augment frozen models. Experiments on eight real-world benchmarks with four backbone models report better effectiveness and efficiency, and show that the codebooks transfer across backbones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decouple trend and seasonal signals into residual codebooks for retrieval augmentation of frozen TSFMs, reporting experiments on eight benchmarks with four backbones and cross-backbone tra

entry.title: Quantum key exchange built on public quantum money, showing it may need weaker assumptions than one-way functions.
entry.summary: Quantum Key Exchange from Public Quantum Money arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper fully characterizes two-message quantum key exchange (2QKE) and shows that everlasting-secure 2QKE, standard 2QKE, efficiently-verifiable state puzzles, and one-time secure quantum-signature schemes are equivalent. Since efficiently-verifiable state puzzles may be weaker than one-way functions, 2QKE may also be weaker than one-way functions. The work further shows that one-shot signatures and related public-key unclonable primitives imply these puzzles, and gives a quantum public-key encryption construction with an added certified freeze functionality. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show four primitives are equivalent to two-message QKE and propose a potentially weaker assumption than one-way functions.

entry.title: Routes of Reasoning: Controlling Overthinking in MoE Models at Test Time
entry.summary: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether the routers in Mixture-of-Experts models reveal the behaviors a model uses during reasoning, such as planning, verifying, and concluding. The authors label reasoning traces by behavior and show that router signals predict these labels nearly as well as residual-stream probes while using fewer features. They then edit expert router scores during inference to reduce overthinking. Across four models and four benchmarks, the median reduction in generated tokens is 30.4%, with accuracy dropping by no more than 0.5 percentage points. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use MoE router scores as a training-free handle on reasoning behaviors, reporting a 30.4% median token reduction across four models and four benchmarks.

entry.title: Does a trial simulator understand what the drug does? An intervention-blind test on 7,207 trials
entry.summary: Does Your Trial Simulator Know What the Drug Does? An Intervention-Blind Test of Interventional Validity on 7,207 Registered Trials arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a measurement of whether patient world models can truly simulate the effect of an intervention in clinical trials. The authors build 9,996 audited within-trial contrasts from 30,119 phase 2/3 trials with posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov, and compare each simulator against an intervention-blind reference model to score how much its accuracy depends on knowing the tested intervention. A gradient-boosting simulator trained on registry data has negative interventional skill, while a frontier language model reading only the registered protocol scores 0.20, and smaller models sit near the limit of detection. ★★★★ Notable: The authors measure counterfactual skill of patient world models via an intervention-blind reference across 9,996 contrasts from 7,207 trials.

entry.title: Convergence Study of Gradient Temporal-Difference Learning with Regularized Corrections and Eligibility Traces
entry.summary: On Convergence of Gradient Temporal-Difference Learning with Regularized Corrections and Eligibility Traces arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies convergence of temporal-difference (TD) learning, a core reinforcement learning method, for TDRC(λ), a regularized-correction variant. The authors prove convergence under diminishing stepsizes and non-i.i.d. off-policy data, with state-dependent and history-dependent λ parameters. They also propose TDRC(λ)-Huber, which reduces sensitivity to large Bellman errors while keeping the same fixed point. When the mean TD matrix is positive stable, both constrained algorithms converge under sufficiently strong regularization without requiring positive definiteness. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend TDRC convergence theory to eligibility traces and non-i.i.d. off-policy data, and propose a Huber-based variant with stability analysis.

entry.title: Complete Characterization of q-Ary 2-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
entry.summary: A Complete Characterization of q-Ary 2-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies when codewords of a fixed weight in doubly-extended Reed-Solomon codes form q-ary 2-designs. It gives an exact criterion: the number of r-subsets of nonzero field elements with a given product is independent of that product if and only if gcd(r, q-1)=1. Applying this to minimum-weight codewords, the authors show they form a q-ary 2-design exactly when gcd(k-1, q-1)=1. They also show that for MDS codes this property at minimum weight extends to all nonzero weights. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete characterization of q-ary 2-designs in doubly-extended Reed-Solomon codes via an exact product-counting criterion over F_q^*.

entry.title: Functional inequalities derived from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
entry.summary: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a Bayesian information-theoretic framework for proving functional inequalities for log-concave measures. It shows that Φ-Sobolev inequalities are equivalent to lower bounds on Bayes risk for estimating functions of a variable observed through Gaussian noise. This yields a simple proof of the O(n^{1/2}) Poincaré constant bound and an improved log-Sobolev bound for subgaussian measures. The authors also recast the shared structure of three recent proofs of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture using low-degree MMSE tools. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish an equivalence between Φ-Sobolev inequalities and Bayesian estimation lower bounds, reporting an improved log-Sobolev constant bound of n^{1/4}.

entry.title: How file parsing can mislead language models about Office documents, and how to fix it
entry.summary: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper shows that large language models usually read text extracted from Office documents' OOXML files, which can differ from what a human sees on screen. By analyzing widely used extractors, the authors identify 19 channels where hidden content is read and 12 where visible content is dropped. They build five attacks that make models interpret documents differently from human reviewers, and these attacks mislead all eight tested chat assistants and coding agents. The authors also propose Prism, a lightweight defense that reconstructs the human view from the OOXML specification and generalizes to unseen payloads. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically show divergence between office document extraction and human view, build five injection-free attacks, report all eight tested assistants and agents are misled, and propose t

entry.title: A mechanism for one-sided matching that keeps total travel distance low using only ranked preferences, with a new sublinear distortion bound.
entry.summary: Sublinear Metric Distortion for Matching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies metric distortion in one-sided matching, where n agents are matched to n items in an unknown metric space and the mechanism sees only each agent's ranking of items by distance. The authors give a mechanism with distortion O(n^{log_4 3}), the first sublinear bound, improving on the O(n) guarantee of Random Serial Dictatorship. Their approach builds a partial matching from truncated Random Serial Dictatorship or Probabilistic Serial, then completes it with a new general cluster completion algorithm. The paper also tightens the distortion bounds for those two rules and improves lower bounds for truthful mechanisms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first sublinear distortion bound, O(n^{log_4 3}), for one-sided matching, improving the long-standing O(n) bound via truncated mechanisms and cluster completion.

entry.title: Self-supervised learning of shared latent spaces for neural operators (a reusable function representation trained without labels)
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper pre-trains a functional autoencoder on synthesized analytic functions, with no solver or labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds. The resulting latent space is frozen and reused across tasks, so neural operators train on cached embeddings. Across 28 tasks in fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, acoustics, Helmholtz and Poisson equations, the authors report accuracy that can exceed end-to-end architectures, with higher throughput and lower memory use. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decouple representation and operator learning via a self-supervised frozen latent space, reporting gains over end-to-end models on 28 PDE tasks with large memory savings.

entry.title: Male abstraction bias: how abstract concepts link to men in internet culture and AI language models
entry.summary: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines tens of thousands of single and multi-word expressions across internet text and images, finding that more abstract concepts are more associated with men. The pattern replicates across languages and extends to grammar, with verbs and adverbs being more abstract and more male-coded. The bias also appears in free association responses from both humans and AI, suggesting it is both internalized and reproduced algorithmically. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that abstractness and male association link across concept space, grammar, and AI free-association, replicated across languages using large internet corpora and images.

entry.title: Can language models tell which constraints should be grouped together?
entry.summary: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how to choose which groups of constraint families to convexify in a mixed-integer program, where some families strengthen the linear relaxation only when applied together. The authors prove that methods observing only bounds need many evaluations to find such hidden groups, and propose JointDW, which combines language-model predictions with a staged search and a one-pass lookahead. On MIPLIB-NL models, the strongest language models identify these groups about as often as the lookahead, and reasoning roughly doubles accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a covering-number lower bound for finding hidden constraint groups and test a staged search with language-model predictions on MIPLIB-NL models.

entry.title: Explaining Information Flow Downgrading Through the Real–Ideal Paradigm
entry.summary: Demystifying Information Flow Downgrading using the Real--Ideal Paradigm arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper adapts the real–ideal paradigm, a cryptography-derived approach to security specification, into a new semantic framework for language-based security. The framework captures existing definitions such as noninterference as well as downgrading-related properties like robust declassification and nonmalleable information flow. The authors show that an information-flow type system for a while-language supporting downgrading enforces these properties, and that its correctness is characterized as a real–ideal simulation. All results are formalized in the Rocq prover and publicly available. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bring the real-ideal paradigm into language security semantics, unifying downgrading information-flow properties, with type-system correctness formalized in Rocq.

entry.title: VIPBench: A Benchmark for Matching Speaker Models to How Listeners Hear Voice Identity
entry.summary: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces VIPBench, a benchmark built from 124,876 same-or-different judgments by 1,290 listeners on 9,800 recording pairs from 100 public figures, including real recordings, text-to-speech voice clones, and morphs. It defines four tasks for measuring how well speaker-representation models align with human identity perception. Evaluating eleven public speech models, the authors find listeners judged a clone and a real recording of the same speaker to be different people in 41% of responses, and no model reaches the noise ceiling. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors evaluate speaker models against 124,876 human same-or-different judgments on real, cloned, and morphed speech, comparing eleven models.

entry.title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games: how a learning agent can resist manipulation and keep low regret when both players face budget constraints
entry.summary: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies repeated general games over T rounds between a utility-maximizing optimizer and a learning agent, where budget constraints link the players' decisions across rounds. The authors give an efficient, budget-feasible learning algorithm under which any adaptive optimizer earns at most BSE·T+O(√T) in expectation, and the learner has O(√T) regret when the optimizer plays a fixed mixed strategy. The algorithm relies on two novel forms of calibrated forecasts, which can be constructed in polynomial time by simulating online gradient ascent. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a budget-feasible learner with non-manipulability and low stochastic regret, using two new calibration notions and a polynomial-time forecast construction.

entry.title: Optimal mixing rate of random matrix walks for building hidden-key matrices over large finite fields
entry.summary: Optimal Marginal Mixing for Transvection-Based Trapdoored Matrices over Large Fields arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies trapdoored matrices, pseudorandom matrices that allow fast matrix-vector multiplication when the secret key is known, generated by short random transvection walks on SL_n(F_q). The authors show that the worst-case time for any nonempty set of matrix entries to approach its stationary marginal distribution is Θ(|S| + n log(n/ε)), which is asymptotically optimal. They also give concrete bounds for n ≥ 256 and propose efficient, parallelizable, and universal trapdoored matrix constructions under a conjectured pseudorandomness assumption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report asymptotically optimal Θ(|S|+n log(n/ε)) mixing for transvection walks and claim the first finite-field trapdoored matrices with inverse trapdoors.

entry.title: Lost in Pooling or Out of Reach? Diagnosing Spatial Left/Right Failures in Vision-Language Similarity
entry.summary: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Contrastive vision-language models perform near chance on left/right spatial relations. The paper identifies two causes: the relation may remain in the pooled embedding but be unreachable by native image-text similarity, or pooling may discard it while dense patch features retain it. The authors propose a parameter-free, query-conditioned spatial moment that recomputes geometry from the patch grid and stores it beside the native embedding. On a 118,287-image index it raises left/right pairwise accuracy to 0.81–0.96 while reproducing the native ranking for queries that name no relation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate two causes of spatial relation failure and repair both with one readout, reporting gains across ten encoders and a 118,287-image index.

entry.title: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models
entry.summary: Near-Minimax Sample Complexity for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Generative Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how many samples multi-objective reinforcement learning needs when reward preferences are chosen only after data collection. For finite discounted decision processes with unknown transitions and a generative model, the authors find near-minimax sample complexity that is logarithmic in the number of objectives and saturates at the number of states. Matching lower bounds are also provided, up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give near-minimax sample complexity for multi-objective RL under generative models, with matching upper and lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: A unified method for combining training datasets and exactly removing their influence from machine learning models
entry.summary: A Unified Framework for Training-Dataset Aggregation and Exact Machine Unlearning via Gibbs Probability Measures arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies three operations on Gibbs probability measures: renormalization, normalized log-linear combination, and nesting, and gives explicit expressions for the objective functions, reference measures, and regularization factors of the resulting measures. When the reference measures are probability measures, these operations are given geometric interpretations involving Pythagorean identities and exponential geodesics. The authors show that nesting and normalized log-linear combination are equivalent, and apply this to Gibbs algorithms so that models trained on local datasets can be combined into models trained on the aggregated data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify three Gibbs measure operations, prove nesting equals normalized log-linear combination, and apply this to dataset aggregation and exact unlearning.

entry.title: Tight lower bounds for high-order smooth, uniformly convex minimization
entry.summary: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order Hölder Smoothness and Uniform Convexity arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper establishes tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match, i.e., q = p + ν. It shows that any deterministic algorithm using derivatives up to order p needs a number of oracle calls of order Ω of the stated form to reduce an initial optimality gap Δ0 to ε. The bound matches the known upper bound and serves as a higher-order uniformly convex analogue of Nesterov's first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight lower bound matching the upper bound for matched high-order Hölder smoothness and uniform convexity, via a new multiscale construction.

entry.title: From Claws to Conferences: Device-Independent Key Agreement Without Non-Signaling Assumptions
entry.summary: From Claws to Conferences: Device-Independent Key Agreement Beyond Non-Signaling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a device-independent conference key agreement protocol that lets a group of users establish a shared secret key without trusting the internal operation of their quantum devices. Unlike earlier protocols, it removes the requirement that device components not communicate during each round, treating all interfaces and their communication as one untrusted device. Assuming the Learning With Errors problem is hard for quantum algorithms with quantum advice during execution, the authors prove finite-size security against coherent attacks. The final key remains secret even if Learning With Errors is later broken after the protocol ends. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a DI-CKA protocol without non-signaling, lifting claw states to GHZ-correlated multipartite states with a finite-size coherent-attack proof.

entry.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Approximating Energy in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Spin Glass Model
entry.summary: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses approximating the maximum energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass model. It introduces GEG-IAMP, an algorithm whose total work is polynomial in both the dimension N and the inverse accuracy 1/ε, with a finite-size probabilistic guarantee. The method replaces the Onsager correction with Reeves's coupling construction and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into O(1/ε) matrix-vector products. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first SK maximum-energy approximation with work polynomial in both N and 1/ε, plus a finite-size guarantee.

entry.title: A paper on which noisy Boolean function is most informative about a hidden bit string
entry.summary: On the most informative Boolean function under noise arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies a problem in information theory: a uniform random bit string X is passed through a channel that flips each bit independently with probability p, producing Y, and a random bit C is computed from Y. The authors prove that the mutual information between C and X is at most that between the first bit of Y and X, for all p in [0,1]. This settles a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the 2013 Courtade-Kumar conjecture, showing the mutual information bound holds for all flip probabilities.

entry.title: A training-free interface connecting DNA models to frozen language models
entry.summary: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models arXiv · Oct 17, 2026This paper introduces socket, a method that links the Evo 2 DNA foundation model to frozen large language models without training a connector. It fits a closed-form ridge regression from DNA features to each host model's representation of gene symbols, names, and descriptions. On the GeneHop five-way multiple-choice benchmark, real DNA outperforms shuffled DNA on all four tested hosts, and the gains survive Holm correction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a closed-form ridge plug linking frozen DNA and language models beats shuffled-DNA controls on four hosts.

entry.title: Tighter Approximation and Competition Bounds for Simple Auctions
entry.summary: A Bulow-Klemperer Theorem for Bundling and Improved Approximation Bounds for Simple Auctions arXiv · Oct 18, 2026The paper studies simple auctions for one additive buyer whose values for several items are independent. For regular items, it proves that grand-bundle second-price revenue with two bidders lies between optimal revenue and twice bundling revenue, which is tight and answers an open question. For general independent items, it improves the approximation factor from 6 and 5.2 to 2.645, and raises the known lower bound from 2 to 2.11. ★★★★★ Notable: For independent regular items the authors show REV≤BSPA₂≤2BREV, answering an open question of Beyhaghi et al.; for general items they report a 2.645 approximation and a lower bound above 2.11.

entry.title: Pareto-optimal Scheduling with Predictions: a paper on single-machine job scheduling that balances trust in predictions against worst-case performance.
entry.summary: Pareto-optimal Non-Clairvoyant Scheduling with Predictions arXiv · Oct 23, 2026The paper studies preemptive single-machine scheduling where a prediction of job order or sizes is available, with the goal of minimizing total completion time. The authors exactly determine the best possible trade-off between consistency and robustness for deterministic algorithms. They give a greedy algorithm achieving this trade-off and prove a matching lower bound. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize the optimal consistency-robustness tradeoff for deterministic algorithms, reporting 1+ε consistency with ε^{-1/2}+1/6+O(√ε) robustness, versus prior Θ(1/ε).

entry.title: A complete addition formula for twisted Edwards curves, a cryptographic curve family
entry.summary: Complete Addition Law for Twisted Edwards Curves IACR ePrint · Nov 2, 2026The paper constructs complete addition formulas in extended coordinates for twisted Edwards curves, valid for every pair of rational points under specified conditions. It analyses the exceptional fibres using a difference morphism and gives full and mixed evaluation schedules. The authors compare operation costs across cases, and state that doubling cost does not depend on the choice of coefficient. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct complete addition laws for twisted Edwards curves, characterize exceptional fibres, prove existence over odd finite fields, and report operation costs.

entry.title: Communication complexity of secure MPC from a random oracle, including quantum variants
entry.summary: On the (Quantum) Communication Complexity of Secure MPC from a Random Oracle IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the communication complexity of information-theoretically secure multi-party computation when only symmetric-key assumptions are available, modeled as a random oracle. For MPC with preprocessing, the authors prove that the known lower bound still holds in this model, so a random oracle cannot reduce online communication. For honest-majority MPC they give an Ω(|C|) lower bound and a matching construction for degree-2 polynomials, including inner products, when n = O(log λ). The paper also analyzes protocols that use quantum communication or a quantum-accessible random oracle. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend MPC communication lower bounds to the random oracle model, match them with a degree-2 construction, and study quantum communication savings and their costs.

entry.title: Tight depth lower bounds for amplifying pseudorandom generator stretch
entry.summary: Tight Depth Lower Bounds for Stretch Amplification IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies the depth overhead of stretch amplification for pseudorandom generators in the black-box model. It shows that black-box constructions with d adaptive phases satisfy an upper bound on output length M, implying the standard repeated-composition amplification is essentially optimal. The results also yield tight depth lower bounds for black-box PRF constructions from PRGs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight depth lower bounds for black-box stretch amplification of PRGs, extending to PRFs, Avoid, and an oracle separation.

entry.title: Recovering master keys from the WBSLT white-box AES design by quotienting redundant lookup tables
entry.summary: Quotienting Redundant Tables: Practical Master-Key Recovery from WBSLT White-Box AES IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026This paper is a cryptanalysis of WBSLT, a white-box AES design presented at NDSS 2026. It shows that the joint output of first-round TypeII lookup tables has an exact 16 × 16 quotient, which reveals the nibble partition of each AES input byte. Using public tables and traces of chosen encoded inputs, the authors report recovering the master key in the tested instances. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use an exact quotient of public lookup tables to recover WBSLT white-box AES master keys, reporting full recovery across 200 general instances and variants.

entry.title: Cryptanalysis of MinRank 2.0: Reassessing Attacks on the MinRank Problem
entry.summary: Cryptanalysis of MinRank 2.0 IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026This paper revisits attacks on MinRank, the hard problem underlying several post-quantum schemes such as the Mirath signature and multivariate schemes like UOV and MAYO. The authors improve the kernel-search attack, lowering its cost by 3 to 6 bits on Mirath parameters and solving Courtois challenge D, open since 2001. They also show that existing complexity estimates for the Kipnis–Shamir attack are inaccurate and give corrected figures. Finally, they extend the Support-Minors and Minors modelings with field equations, which lowers their estimates over small fields. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors improve kernel-search MinRank attacks, report solving open Courtois challenge D, and correct Kipnis-Shamir complexity estimates affecting several post-quantum schemes.

entry.title: The Fairest of Them All: Fair Leader Election Secure Under Two Corruption Models
entry.summary: The Fairest of Them All: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Leader Election IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to pick a random leader fairly from n parties. It introduces best-of-both-worlds (BoBW) fairness: a small number of corrupt parties cannot bias the result, and a larger number still cannot improve their collective chances or reduce any honest party's chances. The authors present a protocol for t_S + t_GT < n, prove it optimal via a generalization of Cleve's impossibility, and give a protocol for the perfect-security setting. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new best-of-both-worlds fairness notion, give a protocol, and report a matching optimality proof with a generalized Cleve impossibility.

entry.title: Leakage-tolerant secure computation without leakage-free setup
entry.summary: Leakage-Tolerant Computation without Leakage-Free Setup IACR ePrint · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies leakage-tolerant multi-party computation, where leakage from honest parties' internal states reveals no more than their inputs and outputs already do. In a computational model assuming only augmented non-committing encryption, the authors show that every adaptively well-formed functionality admits a semi-honest leakage-tolerant protocol without leakage-free preprocessing or a common reference string. Under the decisional Diffie-Hellman assumption, this extends to malicious security in the CRS model for all deterministic functionalities.
